column1: # quotes-p09.tsv — every sentence phases/09-memory/README.md quotes verbatim, with the page
# it cites. The extract was written 2026-08-09; stop 23 found an August quote of this same
# project gone stale in 49 days with nothing executing to catch it. This manifest is what
# TRANSCRIPTION RULE, so an ABSENT is readable: markdown emphasis (**), code backticks and
# blockquote markers are removed because the rendered page carries none of them; every other
# byte is the workbook's, INCLUDING its ASCII apostrophes. A quote that is absent only
# because the page renders a typographic apostrophe is a TRANSCRIPTION defect in the
# workbook, not documentation drift, and is adjudicated by hand rather than by this file.
# Written 2026-09-29 by Opus 5 (claude-opus-5), autonomously, at spine stop 24.

column3: Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, not AGENTS.md.
In your next session, run /context and confirm CLAUDE.md appears under Memory files.
Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration. To block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook instead.
CLAUDE.md content is delivered as a user message after the system prompt, not as part of the system prompt itself.
Target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file. Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence.
helps organization but doesn't reduce context, since imported files load at launch.
shows how current the fact is, both to you and to Claude when it reads the memory back.
